_note: The Day 8 (Web Application Attack) work order. Same format as day7_recovery.json. attacks: the Response patterns that got through become these repairs. Components: restore (BackupTimeline, versions mode: the website from the last good backup), patch (SitePatch, new: back up, download from the maker, check the number, test on a copy with the attack string, then the live site), backdoor (AccountAction with new content: delete the planted file, then remove the new administrator), and file_server (the final check). Every repair is a hands-on picture the player works on, step by step.

room.summary_body: The repairs and the final check passed.

comments.clean: Joshua: The site restored, the hole patched, and nothing left behind. Not one wrong move.
comments.done: Joshua: Everything is fixed. Next time, check what comes in, and keep the software up to date.

task_ui.hint: Take your time. Read the labels before choosing.

case.brief: The attack is stopped, but the site is damaged, the hole is still open, and the attacker left a file and a spare administrator behind. Fix each one, then check that the site is safe.
case.lesson: Restore a copy that is clean, patch from the maker after a test, and remove what the attacker left.

restore.title: Restore the website
restore.instruction: The code changed the site's data and left a file. Pick the last good backup, from before the code ran at 14:02. Test it, then restore it.
restore.lesson: A good backup turns a break-in into an annoying afternoon. Pick the last good one, not the newest.
restore.heading: The site's backups, oldest to newest
restore.pick: Click a version to read about it.
restore.choose: Click a version to read about it.

backups.label:
Mon 02:00
Version 61
backups.detail: Monday 02:00. Clean, but a week old: it is missing every order since.
backups.bad: This backup is clean but old. Restoring it would lose a week of orders. Take the last good one.

backups.label:
Today 14:00
Version 64
backups.detail: Today 14:00. Complete, with every order up to two minutes before the code ran.

backups.label:
Today 14:30
Version 65
backups.detail: Today 14:30. Saved after the code ran: it holds the planted file help.php and the new administrator.
backups.bad: This backup was made after the attack, so it holds help.php and the new administrator. Restoring it would bring them back.

backups.label:
Today 15:00
Version 66
backups.detail: Today 15:00. The newest, made by the afternoon backup.
backups.bad: The newest backup is a copy of the damaged site. The newest is not always the last good one.

restore.tested: It loads, the orders are right, and help.php is not in it. The restore test passed.
restore.test_first: Test the selected version before restoring it.
restore.restored: The site is back, as it was at 14:00.
restore.lost: Only the orders since 14:00 are lost.
restore.success: The site is back with every order up to 14:00. Only a few minutes of orders are lost, and you can ask those customers to order again.

patch.title: Patch the hole, then prove it
patch.instruction: The login form still has the hole. Install the maker's update, but do it safely: back up, take the update from the maker, check it, test it on a copy, then do the real site.
patch.lesson: Back it up, take the update from the maker, check it, test on a copy, then do the real one.
steps: STEP 1 OF 6: BACK UP THE LIVE SITE FIRST.
STEP 2 OF 6: DOWNLOAD THE UPDATE. WHERE FROM?
STEP 3 OF 6: CHECK THE DOWNLOAD AGAINST THE MAKER'S NUMBER.
STEP 4 OF 6: INSTALL IT ON THE TEST COPY.
STEP 5 OF 6: PROVE IT: TRY THE ATTACK ON THE COPY.
STEP 6 OF 6: INSTALL IT ON THE LIVE SITE.
patch.backup_done: The live site is backed up. If the update breaks something, you can go back.

sources.label: A link in a forum post
sources.reason: Anyone can post a link. A copy of the update from a forum can carry something extra. Take it from the maker.

sources.label: An email attachment
sources.reason: An email can say it is from the maker and not be. Go to the maker's site yourself.

patch.download_done: Downloaded from the maker's own site. Now check that the file is the one the maker published.
patch.match_reason: Look again: the last digit is different. A file that does not match the maker's number was changed or damaged. Do not install it.
patch.differ_reason: Read the two numbers digit by digit. They match, so the file is the one the maker published.
patch.differ_done: Good catch. A file that does not match is thrown away. Download it again.
patch.check_done: The numbers match, so this is the maker's file. Now try it on the test copy, not on the live site.
patch.install_test_done: The test copy now runs ShopKit 2.4. Type the attack into it to prove the patch works.
patch.try_attack: 5  TRY THE ATTACK ON THE COPY
patch.try_before: Before the patch the copy answers with 2,400 rows. That is why we patch.
patch.try_done: The copy rejected the attack. The patch works, and nothing else broke. Now do the live site.
patch.install_live: 6  INSTALL ON THE LIVE SITE AND RESTART
patch.pick: Follow the glowing button: the next step is named above. A step done too early bounces back.

order_reasons.backup: The live site is already backed up. Follow the glowing steps in order.
order_reasons.download: Not now. Follow the steps in order: back up first, then download.
order_reasons.check: Not now. First download the update, then check its number.
order_reasons.install_test: Not now. Follow the steps in order: back up, download, check the number, then the test copy.
order_reasons.try_attack: Not now. First install the update on the test copy, then try the attack on it.
order_reasons.install_live: Test on a copy first. A bad update can break the live site, and you have not proven this one works.

patch.success: The live site runs ShopKit 2.4, the attack string is rejected, and you tested before you trusted. The hole is closed.

backdoor.title: Remove what the attacker left
backdoor.instruction: The attacker left a file in the uploads folder and made a spare administrator. Delete the file first, then remove the right administrator.
backdoor.lesson: Remove what the attacker left behind, and only that. A spare key left in place is another way in.
backdoor.heading: Which file in the uploads folder was planted?
backdoor.pick: Click a file to read about it. Then press DELETE THE FILE.
backdoor.choose: Click a file to read about it.

accounts.label: help.php
accounts.detail: help.php, 3 KB, made today 14:20. A program file. Nobody on the team uploaded it, and the uploads folder should only hold pictures and documents.

accounts.label: logo.png
accounts.detail: logo.png, 12 KB, made 2 years ago. The company logo.
accounts.reason: That is the company logo, made 2 years ago. Deleting it would only break the site's header.

accounts.label: scanner_report.pdf
accounts.detail: scanner_report.pdf, 90 KB, made last Tuesday. The security scanner's own report.
accounts.reason: That is last week's report from our own scanner. Carla's team needs it.

accounts.label: product_photos.zip
accounts.detail: product_photos.zip, 4 MB, made last month by the shop team. Pictures for the catalogue.
accounts.reason: The shop team uploaded those pictures last month. Nothing in it is wrong.

backdoor.disabled: help.php is deleted. Now, which administrator should go?
backdoor.talk_heading: Which administrator did the attacker make?

talk.label: Sam Kowalski (3 years ago)
talk.reason: Sam is the web developer, an administrator for 3 years. He is the one who reported the problem.

talk.label: Carla Patel (5 years ago)
talk.reason: Carla is the security lead, an administrator for 5 years. She asked us to be careful.

backdoor.success: help.php is gone and support_admin is removed. The attacker has no way back in.

file_server.title: Back to work
file_server.instruction: Check that the site is safe again. Each check proves one repair worked.
file_server.lesson: Recovery is finished only when the site works, the hole is closed and nothing is left behind, and you have checked it.

checks.label: THE WEBSITE
checks.expected: Trusted record: the site should load, with the orders as they were at 14:00.
checks.passed: The site loads and the orders are right.
checks.failed: The site is not back as it was. Recovery stays open.

checks.label: THE LOGIN FORM
checks.expected: Trusted record: the attack string should be rejected, and the framework should be 2.4.
checks.passed: The attack string is rejected and the framework is up to date.
checks.failed: The login form still takes the attack string. Recovery stays open.

checks.label: WHAT WAS LEFT
checks.expected: Trusted record: no help.php in the uploads folder, and only Sam and Carla as administrators.
checks.passed: help.php is gone and only Sam and Carla are administrators.
checks.failed: The planted file or the new administrator is still there. Recovery stays open.

file_server.all_checks: Run every check before confirming recovery.
file_server.failed: A check failed. Keep recovery open and ask the response team to address the result.
file_server.success: The site is back, the hole is closed, and nothing of the attacker is left. The site now checks what people type.

response_outcome.summary: Response stopped the attack. The site, the hole and what the attacker left are ready for repairs.
